speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse. Also, have you experienced any swelling, locking, or a popping sound when the injury occurred?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome. Based on your recent history of pivoting during volleyball, the location of your pain (likely around or behind the kneecap), and the worsening nature of the symptoms, this is the most likely cause. We will confirm this by checking if your pain increases when you squat or walk down stairs, and I will request an X-Ray to rule out any fractures or severe structural damage.
